prediction_ref.short_label: AI-accelerator equities re-rate lower on the next in-line ASIC print by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Direct continuation of the prediction's own origin event. The June 7 thesis was anchored on Broadcom's in-line Q3 AI-semi guide (~$16B vs ~$17.2B consensus) sending AVGO down ~15% and dragging Micron, Intel, AMD and Nvidia lower for two sessions on expectations-asymmetry rather than a miss. Today's chip story is the other side of that same washout: Monday June 8 snapped back, Intel +8.5% and Micron +9%, recovering from the prior Friday when the Nasdaq fell 4.2% (its worst day since April) and the chip index shed roughly $1 trillion on that same Broadcom guidance plus memory/smartphone-demand fears. Desks characterized Friday's drop as a liquidity-driven washout rather than a thesis change, which is consistent with the prediction's claim that these names trade on a raised bar - but the evidence is a reversal, not a fresh in-line print taking the group down again, so it neither confirms nor refutes the forward landing. Notably the rebound rotated leadership toward US-manufacturing catalysts (Alphabet-Intel foundry, Nvidia 18A evaluation) rather than the merchant-GPU names that led the prior run, a different mix of names carrying the same AI-capex story.

prediction_ref.short_label: US open-weights model crosses 54 on Artificial Analysis Index by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 4 prediction tracks the US open-weights frontier closing the index gap to the top Chinese open model, on the strength of frequent frontier-scale open releases from US labs. Today's DiffusionGemma launch is a fresh data point on US open-weights cadence - Google shipped a 26B Mixture-of-Experts (3.8B active) open model under Apache 2.0 on June 10, built on the Gemma 4 backbone. It moves the open frontier on a different axis than the prediction's marker, though: the release is about a text-diffusion decoding paradigm and up-to-4x faster local inference, not a higher Artificial Analysis Index score, and Google is explicit that DiffusionGemma's output quality trails standard autoregressive Gemma 4 and steers production work back to the autoregressive model. So it is supporting evidence that US labs keep publishing open weights aggressively, but it does not itself advance the index-score landing - no Artificial Analysis Index figure is reported, and the quality-tradeoff framing cuts against a frontier-quality reading.

prediction_ref.short_label: Coding-agent frameworks ship goal-grounded completion verification by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 7 prediction is that coding-agent harnesses converge on harness-layer gating that forces the agent to clear a trusted check before reporting done, rather than trusting a self-authored proxy. Today's datasette-agent 0.2a0 ships an adjacent harness-layer control: a ToolContext.ask_user primitive that lets a tool suspend the run to ask the operator a yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text question instead of guessing, plus a save_query tool that writes agent-generated SQL only after explicit human approval. This is the same instinct - move the trust boundary into the harness and refuse to let the agent self-certify a result - but the mechanism is a durable human-in-the-loop approval/clarification gate rather than the prediction's automated run-the-real-target verification. It is a fresh open-source data point on harness-level completion discipline, supporting the broad direction without satisfying the specific goal-grounded, machine-checked marker the prediction names.

bridge.narrative: The datasette-agent 0.2a0 alpha pushes the trust boundary into the harness, adding an ask_user primitive that suspends the run for an operator yes/no or free-text answer and a save_query tool that commits agent-written SQL only after explicit approval. bridge.remaining_gap: The gate here is human-in-the-loop approval; the marker still needs an automated run-the-real-target check that machine-verifies completion against the stated goal.
